name: Star_System_Navigation

questions.question: How does navigation data (star charts, safe routes, shortcut paths) function as a tradeable information commodity that creates a cartographer career path?
questions.answer: Navigation data is high-value information. A full star chart costs 500 credits from NPC cartographers — or a player can discover routes for free then sell the data. A shortcut saving 2 hours has economic value: buyers save fuel costs. This creates a cartographer career where explorers generate revenue selling route data, not trading physical goods.

questions.question: Does navigating between star systems tell the story of charting the unknown — plotting courses by stellar cartography, discovering new systems, and leaving the player's mark on the map?
questions.answer: Star navigation tells an explorer's story: each jump is a step into the unknown, each unknown system is a blank page, each named discovery is a authored chapter — the player writes their own odyssey onto the galaxy.

questions.question: Can the player plot a course between star systems using the star chart with clear visualization of waypoints, fuel requirements, and travel time -- without needing external tools or spreadsheets?
questions.answer: Star chart shows reachable systems highlighted within current fuel range. Click-to-plot draws a route line with fuel stops. Each leg shows distance (LY), fuel cost, and ETA. Route confirms with one button. No manual coordinate entry.

questions.question: Does the player's discovered star chart data, plotted routes, and visited systems need to persist?
questions.answer: Yes. Star chart state is persistent exploration progress: discovered star positions (x,y,z in galaxy), visited system IDs (set), plotted routes (source-destination pairs), navigation waypoints. Heavy save data. Written on discovery or route plot.

questions.question: Does the star navigation system use real stellar physics (proper motion, parallax, spectral classification, Hertzsprung-Russell diagram) or is it abstracted?
questions.answer: Abstracted with real references. Star positions are world-aligned and fixed (no proper motion simulation). Spectral classification (OBAFGKM) is used for star color and temperature display. The HR diagram is shown in educational annotations but does not drive the simulation.
